entries.title: NGOs Co-ordination Board v EG & 4 others
entries.principle: Administrative action must be lawful, reasonable and procedurally fair; the analysis asks whether the decision was unreasonable, unlawful or disproportionate.
entries.facts: A challenge to the registration of an NGO advocating for LGBTQ+ rights.
entries.holding: Administrative action must be lawful, reasonable and procedurally fair; the analysis asks whether the decision was unreasonable, unlawful or disproportionate.

entries.title: Saisi & 7 others v Director of Public Prosecutions & 2 others
entries.principle: Fairness is secured where parties retain meaningful access to remedies capable of review; an administrative process is not unfair merely because it is efficient.
entries.facts: A challenge to the DPP's decision to charge public officials.
entries.holding: Fairness is secured where parties retain meaningful access to remedies capable of review; an administrative process is not unfair merely because it is efficient.

entries.title: Mutheu Agatha Khimulu v Raheem Mehdi Aziz Azad & 4 others
entries.principle: The best interests of the child enshrine the right to parental care; the concept is a primary, not exclusive, consideration to be balanced against competing interests.
entries.facts: A custody dispute involving a child's best interests.
entries.holding: The best interests of the child enshrine the right to parental care; the concept is a primary, not exclusive, consideration to be balanced against competing interests.

entries.title: John Florence Maritime Services Limited & another v Cabinet Secretary for Transport & Infrastructure & 3 others
entries.principle: The justiciable elements of a fair hearing are an opportunity to be heard that is reasonable; administrative determinations are governed by Article 47, not the full trial guarantees of Article 50.
entries.facts: A challenge to the refusal of a maritime licence.
entries.holding: The justiciable elements of a fair hearing are an opportunity to be heard that is reasonable; administrative determinations are governed by Article 47.

entries.title: Attorney General v Kituo Cha Sheria & 7 others
entries.principle: A security measure must be supported by concrete evidence; an encampment directive that is speculative and unsupported by evidence is unlawful.
entries.facts: A challenge to an encampment directive for refugees.
entries.holding: A security measure must be supported by concrete evidence; an encampment directive that is speculative and unsupported by evidence is unlawful.

entries.title: Kandie v Alassane BA & Another
entries.principle: The test for limiting rights is one of reasonableness and justification, requiring a balancing of competing interests rather than a mechanical approach.
entries.facts: A challenge to the deportation of a foreign national on security grounds.
entries.holding: The test for limiting rights is one of reasonableness and justification, requiring a balancing of competing interests rather than a mechanical approach.

entries.title: Judicial Service Commission v Mbalu Mutava & another
entries.principle: Procedural fairness is preserved where the affected person is heard, reasons are given and independent review is available; fairness is balanced with the wider public interest.
entries.facts: A challenge to the removal of a member of the Judicial Service Commission.
entries.holding: Procedural fairness is preserved where the affected person is heard, reasons are given and independent review is available.

entries.title: Refugee Consortium of Kenya & Another (Suing on Behalf of DL (Minor) & 47 Others) v Attorney General & 2 Others
entries.principle: The best interests of the child are not an absolute bar to implementing legitimate national security and refugee control measures; they are a primary consideration to be balanced.
entries.facts: A challenge to the detention and deportation of refugee children.
entries.holding: The best interests of the child are not an absolute bar to implementing legitimate national security and refugee control measures; they are a primary consideration to be balanced.

entries.title: M.S.S. v Belgium and Greece
entries.principle: International protection systems must be practical and effective rather than theoretical or illusory; meaningful access to protection is the governing standard.
entries.facts: A challenge to the detention and living conditions of an asylum seeker in Belgium and Greece.
entries.holding: International protection systems must be practical and effective rather than theoretical or illusory; meaningful access to protection is the governing standard.

entries.title: Institute for Human Rights and Development in Africa v Angola
entries.court: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights
entries.principle: Expulsions and adverse immigration decisions must be subject to effective review mechanisms; the absence of review renders the measure unlawful.
entries.facts: A challenge to the expulsion of aliens from Angola.
entries.holding: Expulsions and adverse immigration decisions must be subject to effective review mechanisms; the absence of review renders the measure unlawful.
entries.judges: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights

entries.title: Suresh v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration)
entries.principle: States may exclude individuals from refugee protection where they are implicated in terrorism or serious threats to national security, provided procedural safeguards are respected.
entries.facts: A challenge to the deportation of a suspected terrorist to Sri Lanka.
entries.holding: States may exclude individuals from refugee protection where they are implicated in terrorism or serious threats to national security, provided procedural safeguards are respected.

entries.title: Kudła v Poland (GC)
entries.court: European Court of Human Rights (Grand Chamber)
entries.principle: Overcrowding and poor conditions of detention may amount to inhuman or degrading treatment where they exceed the threshold of severity, taking account of duration and cumulative effect.
entries.facts: A challenge to overcrowded and poor prison conditions.
entries.holding: Overcrowding and poor conditions of detention may amount to inhuman or degrading treatment where they exceed the threshold of severity, taking account of duration and cumulative effect.
entries.judges: European Court of Human Rights (Grand Chamber)

entries.title: Maaouia v France
entries.principle: Disputes concerning the entry, stay and deportation of aliens do not generally fall within the scope of the right to a fair hearing, provided that effective remedies exist elsewhere in the legal system.
entries.facts: A challenge to the refusal of a residence permit to an alien.
entries.holding: Disputes concerning the entry, stay and deportation of aliens do not generally fall within the scope of the right to a fair hearing, provided that effective remedies exist elsewhere in the legal system.

entries.title: Chahal v United Kingdom
entries.principle: Non-refoulement under the European Convention is absolute, but the narrower protection under the Refugee Convention permits derogations on security grounds where procedural safeguards are respected.
entries.facts: A challenge to the deportation of a Sikh activist to India.
entries.holding: Non-refoulement under the European Convention is absolute, but the narrower protection under the Refugee Convention permits derogations on security grounds where procedural safeguards are respected.

entries.title: Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees
entries.principle: Article 33 (non-refoulement) and its Article 33(2) security exception; Articles 9, 26 and 32.
entries.note: Article 33 (non-refoulement) and its Article 33(2) security exception; Articles 9, 26 and 32.

entries.title: Convention relating to the Status of Refugees
entries.principle: Non-refoulement and the definition of a refugee.
entries.note: Non-refoulement and the definition of a refugee.

entries.title: OAU Convention Governing the Specific Aspects of Refugee Problems in Africa
entries.principle: Article II(3) and Article VIII: exclusion on security grounds and the broader African definition of refugee.
entries.note: Article II(3) and Article VIII: exclusion on security grounds and the broader African definition of refugee.

entries.title: Refugees Act, 2021
entries.principle: Sections 2, 7, 29(4) and 31(1) govern refugee status determination, exclusion, deportation and encampment.
entries.note: Sections 2, 7, 29(4) and 31(1) govern refugee status determination, exclusion, deportation and encampment.

entries.title: UNHCR Guidelines on International Protection
entries.principle: Procedural standards for refugee status determination, including the use of technology.
entries.note: Procedural standards for refugee status determination, including the use of technology.
